values: Favourite displays documents marked as favorite in the user's personal library. The screen allows the user to search, filter by reading status, sort, view progress, open document details, remove a document from favorites, read, edit or delete a document, and navigate to other main screens. Both LOCAL_UPLOAD and REMOTE_URL documents may appear when favorite = true.
Favourite screen design showing navigation, search, status filter and favorite document table.
Overview of Favourite loading, filtering and document actions.
When the user opens Favourite, retrieve documents where favorite = true and display a loading state until the request is completed.
Favorite state is stored in SQL Server.
On success, display only favorite documents and all available list controls.
The page title must be “Favourite”, not “Recent Read” as shown in the supplied mockup.
Display the application name and subtitle in the left navigation area.
Display only; no click action is required in this version.
Highlight Favorites as the active navigation item while SCR-04 is displayed.
Only one menu item may be active. Navigation label may remain plural while the screen title uses Favourite.
When selected, navigate to SCR-01 Dashboard.
When selected, navigate to SCR-02 Library.
When selected, navigate to SCR-03 Recent.
Recent displays documents with reading history.
Allow favorite documents to be searched by title, author or tag.
Case-insensitive; trim leading/trailing spaces; do not search non-favorite documents.
Apply the keyword when the user presses Enter or after an agreed debounce period, then refresh the Favourite list.
Recommended debounce: 300–500 ms if searching while typing.
When the keyword is cleared, restore the list using the remaining filter and sort conditions.
Search, filter and sort conditions may be combined.
Display the Settings icon at the top-right.
Hide or disable it if Settings is outside the project scope.
When Status Filter is selected, display the available reading statuses.
Values: All, UNREAD, READING and COMPLETED.
Apply the selected reading status within favorite documents and refresh the list.
Only one status is assumed in the current design.
Selecting All clears the status condition and displays all favorite documents.
The search keyword and sort condition remain unchanged.
Display only documents where favorite = true.
Every displayed row must show a filled star. The outlined stars in the supplied mockup are inconsistent and must be corrected.
Display the document title. Selecting the title or row opens Book Details.
Long text is truncated with a tooltip; modal behavior may be specified separately.
If empty, display “Unknown author” only when author is optional.
Display lastReadPage / totalPages as a percentage and progress bar.
If totalPages is null or zero, display “—”; clamp to 0–100%.
UNREAD = 0%; READING = 1–99%; COMPLETED = 100%. Mock data showing Unread with 22% must be corrected.
Display up to two tag chips; when more tags exist, display “+N”.
Selecting +N may show all tags in a tooltip/popover.
Display a filled star for every document on this screen.
An outlined star must not remain in the Favourite list.
When the filled star is selected, set favorite = false and remove the document from the current list.
On failure, restore the filled star and keep the row visible. A brief Undo notification is recommended.
When the book icon is selected, open the Read PDF screen at lastReadPage.
Reader screen ID is TBD. Prefer IndexedDB when an offline copy exists.
When the pencil icon is selected, open Add/Edit Document in edit mode.
Add/Edit screen ID is TBD; the selected document data is prefilled.
When the trash icon is selected, display a confirmation dialog before deletion.
No deletion occurs until the user confirms.
Delete the Book record and application-managed copy, then remove it from Favourite, Library and other lists.
Do not delete the user's original device file or remote source. Remove the current browser's IndexedDB copy when present.
Close the confirmation dialog and keep all data unchanged.
Return focus to the delete action.
Selecting BOOK TITLE cycles between ascending and descending title order within favorite documents.
Show the active direction in the header.
Selecting AUTHOR cycles between ascending and descending author order within favorite documents.
Selecting PROGRESS cycles between ascending and descending progress order within favorite documents.
Unavailable progress values are placed last.
If no document is marked favorite, display an empty-state message and a link to SCR-02 Library.
Do not display empty table rows.
If no favorite document matches the active conditions, display a no-result message and Clear search/Reset status actions.
Do not treat this state as a load error.
When loading fails, display an error message and a Retry action.
Do not show stale data as newly loaded data.
When remove-favorite or delete fails, restore the previous row state and show a non-blocking error message.
Do not silently remove the document from the list.
On desktop, display the sidebar, Status Filter and full favorite-document table shown in the design.
Reference design width is approximately 1440 px or greater.
On mobile, collapse navigation and convert each row to a card without horizontal page scrolling.
Place secondary actions in a More menu; maintain touch-friendly targets.
Provide tooltips, keyboard focus and accessible names for Favorite, Read, Delete and Edit icons.
Icons must not be the only programmatic label.
Display the application version in the footer.
Display Online Mode or Offline Mode based on browser connectivity.
Connection mode does not guarantee that every document is available offline.
